items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: maybe as Dizzy said that’s the first thing he’d get for a big band was a good bass player

ctx.x: If you were talking to a group of young musicians, which I know you do a lot, can you describe how you think of your role as a bassist?

Sure. Well I do a lot of teaching and I think that the bass is probably — maybe as Dizzy said that’s the first thing he’d get for a big band was a good bass player, and he’d go from there. And I think it is probably that — I wouldn’t say the most important — but right in there with the drums and the piano and the rhythm, it’s very central. And the feel, the team spirit that you have to develop as a bass player I think is very important. I don’t care about the solos, that can come later. But I always tell bass…
elements that go into it, but mainly being a team player, and kind of maybe subjugating your ego just a little bit, to do it.
